sample_unit: patients (across temporal, domain and geographic validation cohorts)
models_evaluated: Reintubation risk prediction model after cardiac surgery

links.outcome: Discrimination, calibration and precision/recall of reintubation model at new institutions versus development site
links.effect: Optimism-corrected c-statistic fell from 0.77 (temporal) to 0.73 and 0.71 at other sites; Brier scores stayed low (0.044, 0.0149, 0.0152); optimal F1 was low (0.29, 0.13, 0.13).
links.quote: The reintubation model displayed strong discriminative ability and low predictive error within each validation cohort.

links.outcome: Precision and recall of the model at new sites with lower reintubation prevalence
links.effect: At other sites (reintubation rate 1.5%-1.6%), c-statistic was 0.71-0.73 and Brier 0.0149-0.0152, but optimal F1 was only 0.13, indicating poor precision/recall.
links.quote: The model displayed solid discriminative ability (optimism-corrected c-statistic = 0.73) and low predictive error (Brier score = 0.0149) but low precision and recall (Optimal F1 score = 0.13).

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation (temporal, geographic, domain) of an existing predictive risk model for reintubation after cardiac surgery across three medical centers.
